name: Wall Sit
summary: An isometric bodyweight exercise holding a squat posture against a wall to build lower-body endurance, particularly in the quadriceps.

setup: Stand with your back flat against a sturdy, smooth wall.
Step your feet forward roughly two feet from the wall, positioned shoulder-width apart and pointing straight ahead or slightly turned out.
steps: Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor, forming ninety-degree angles at both your hips and knees.
Ensure your knees track directly above your ankles, not extending past your toes.
Press your entire back and head flat against the wall, resting your arms at your sides or across your chest.
Hold this position statically for the target duration, keeping tension in the legs throughout.
Push through your heels and slide back up the wall to stand once finished.
instructions.breathing: Breathe continuously and steadily throughout the hold, avoiding holding your breath against fatigue.

common_faults.fault: Resting hands on the thighs or knees to offload body weight.
common_faults.correction: Keep your arms crossed over your chest or hanging freely at your sides.

common_faults.fault: Setting the feet too close to the wall, causing knees to drift far past the toes and overloading the patellofemoral joint.
common_faults.correction: Step your feet far enough forward so your shins remain vertical when your thighs are parallel.

common_faults.fault: Sitting too high or dropping the hips below knee level.
common_faults.correction: Lower yourself until your hips and knees form clean ninety-degree angles.

precautions: Perform on a non-slip floor surface to prevent the feet from sliding forward during the hold.
